Four circles can be arranged so that every pair intersects in two points, and all of these points are distinct. Such an arrangement exists: for example, four mutually overlapping circles of similar size, placed in general position.

There are C(4,2) = 6 pairs, and each pair contributes at most 2 points, so the maximum is 6 × 2 = 12 points.

Solution A is wrong. It claims opposite circles meet only once, and that more intersections can't be achieved, which is false. Solution B gives the correct count of 12.

WINNER: B
